title: Conditioning on Bob's false special bit leaves Alice's special-bit law unchanged
statement: Fix a positive integer $n$, a deterministic disjointness protocol $p$ on inputs of length $n$, and an achievable value $z$ of the coarse variable $Z = (M, T, X_{<T}, Y_{>T})$. Let $\mu_z$ be the hard distribution conditioned on the fiber $\{Z = z\}$, and suppose that under $\mu_z$ the event that Bob's bit at the special coordinate is $\mathrm{false}$ (that is, $Y_T = \mathrm{false}$) has positive probability. Then the law of Alice's special bit $X_T$ under $\mu_z$ coincides with the law of $X_T$ under $\mu_z$ conditioned further on $\{Y_T = \mathrm{false}\}$.
hypotheses_covered: a deterministic disjointness protocol $p$ on inputs of length $n$
an achievable value $z$ of the $Z$ variable
the event $\{Y_T = \mathrm{false}\}$ has positive probability under the fiber measure $\mu_z$
replaced: Rectangle switching implies the fiber identity $p(X_{T} | Z=z) = p(X_{T} | Z=z, Y_{T}=false)$.
